stem: After minor superficial eye trauma, a client has acute eye pain, tearing, and foreign-body sensation. No retained foreign body is seen, and fluorescein staining highlights a superficial corneal epithelial defect. Which condition is most consistent with these findings?
rationale: Current NCBI StatPearls guidance describes corneal abrasion as superficial disruption of the corneal epithelium after nonpenetrating trauma, commonly causing pain, foreign-body sensation, tearing, photophobia, and redness. Fluorescein staining highlights the epithelial defect. Because the stem states that no retained foreign body is seen and describes a superficial fluorescein-positive epithelial defect, A is the best answer. The findings do not indicate a retained object, penetrating/open-globe injury, or an infectious conjunctivitis pattern.
educational_objective: Recognize a fluorescein-staining superficial corneal epithelial defect after minor trauma as a corneal abrasion.
source_organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI), StatPearls

source_claim_supported: Minor superficial ocular trauma can cause corneal abrasion with pain, foreign-body sensation and tearing; fluorescein staining highlights the corneal epithelial defect.

correction_summary: Resolved the source item's ambiguity between corneal abrasion and retained foreign body by stating that no foreign body is seen and adding the directly supported fluorescein-positive superficial epithelial defect. Replaced weak distractors with clinically adjacent ocular conditions.
audit_findings: A is directly supported by current NCBI guidance. B was a genuine second-answer risk in the source item because sand exposure plus foreign-body sensation can indicate a retained object; the final stem explicitly excludes retained material and adds a fluorescein-positive epithelial defect. C would require signs of penetrating/full-thickness injury not present here. D does not fit the trauma-linked epithelial defect. No treatment regimen, patching rule, healing time, or other unsupported precision is tested. NCSBN 2026 supports the Physiological Adaptation mapping through Pathophysiology and Illness Management.
